headline: Approved Vermont State Merger Committee appointments and consent agenda covering financial reports, hiring recommendations, and prior meeting minutes.
summary: The board approved its consent agenda, including routine financial reports, hiring recommendations, and minutes from prior meetings. It also appointed board members to the Vermont State Merger Committee and heard updates on busing, the budget timeline, strategic plan, and CESA merger study.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including routine financial reports, routine hiring recommendations, and minutes from the 8/4 School Board meeting, 8/11 DEI Committee meeting, and 8/25 Curriculum Committee meeting.
Appointed Lucia Campriello, Kendra Sowers, Jean Waltz, Gary Golden, and Clare Wool to the Vermont State Merger Committee for 2026-2027.

7. Superintendent's Report  
A. Student Recognition: 
BHS Heroes  
At this time, I’d like to ask Daniel Gavin and the BHS Heroes club to join us. Dan Gavin, or 
Herr Gavin as he is called in class, is the German teacher at BHS and he also runs the BHS 
Heroes club. BHS Heroes is a Burlington High School club dedicated to helping and giving 
back to our community.  
They offer a variety of opportunities each year for students to gain volunteer hours and 
increase their involvement in their community. They work with many different community 
organizations, including North End Food Pantry, the Red Cross, Spectrum, and more.  
We are here today to recognize the students in the BHS Heroes club who this summer 
were named the 2025-2026 Vermont Principals Association D1 Food Drive State 
Champions!  
The VPA partnered with Market 32 to create a statewide food drive, offering state 
championships in each athletic division. BHS Heroes joined students from Mt. Abe and 
Bellcate as State Champions. Together, students from across the state brought in more 
than 1,800 food items. The Heroes Club won a $500 gift card to Market 32, which they said 
would be used to buy and donate more food. Anja, Harper, Rowan, Nora, Adele 
We are so proud to have the BHS Heroes as members of our community. Herr Gavin, could 
you introduce your team please? Congratulations, BHS Heroes! Please give our students 
and their fearless leader a round of applause.   
B. Discussion: August Superintendent Reflection 
1. First Days of School – Our 10 Schools are open and running smoothly.  
a. BHS/BTC is off and running. I am really proud of the work Principal Westdijk and 
her leadership team have done to create thoughtful transitions to the new 
building.  
2. Busing – Hearing Concerns about GMT bus trip times from south end to BHS/BTC 
and from ONE to HMS. Working closely with GMT, who is reviewing data. 
3. HMS – Some families are concerned about the #7 buses are leaving at 7:20 and 
7:40, both getting to HMS on time this week. GMT is reviewing ridership and times 
and our team is working with them on this. 
4. BHS/BTC – Two issues – New building and no neighborhood special and hasn’t 
been since we switched to 9:00 start and moved to Macy’s.  
a. GMT added an extra bus at the transit center during peak BHS morning 
commute times to cover potential overflow, and added an extra afternoon 
bus from EMS to the Boys & Girls Club.

b. Because to the transfer they also added an additional security guard 
c. Transit times across various South End addresses for almost all locations 
door-to-door times generally range between 22 and 40 minutes. Returning 
home at 3:15 PM shows nearly identical times. 
d. Adding new routes would require a 3–4 month union bidding process and 
significant extra cost, and I'm not sure how much it would help but we will 
continue monitoring this with GMT.  
3.        Summer Meals Program - Our summer meals program distributed more than 
100,000 meals to children in Chittenden and Grand Isle counties. There was 
overwhelming demand for this service yet again this year. Shout out to Laura La 
Vacca and our School Nutrition team.
